summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis, cirrhosis, and a history of recurrent cholangitis was readmitted for recurrent right upper quadrant abdominal pain and low-grade fever. She had recently completed a course of ertapenem for a prior cholangitis episode. Imaging revealed biliary sludge and a small stone in the gallbladder remnant. An ERCP was performed, which showed no strictures and allowed for removal of sludge from the bile duct. Antibiotics were switched from ertapenem to meropenem for a targeted seven-day course post-procedure. Her symptoms resolved, liver enzymes improved, and she remained afebrile. She was discharged home with plans to continue IV meropenem via her existing PICC line, restart home diuretics, and follow up for lab monitoring and outpatient procedures. Her transplant status remains unchanged.
